It is anyhow observed (see the attachment  “Socio_economic_impact_analysis_16012013”) that the project generates net  positive impacts on the social and economic well-being of the local communities  who derive livelihoods from the project area.  The local population is very poor, they live managing a few of agricultural  activities, with traditional tools and methods. The most problems affecting to  growth of crops are due to lack of water.  The local people are usually cultivating only millet and peanuts, which are the  main crops in the area, with the consequently problems of a diversified diet and  malnutrition, especially for the children.  Jatropha cultivation can be very useful in bringing an agricultural reformation by  revitalizing land use and livelihoods in rural areas, especially for countries  having abundant barren land and poor in other natural endowments; these  projects, in fact, are creating new job opportunities, preventing land  abandonment and reducing in-country migration to the cities. Among the rural  areas already involved in project activities, there has been registered an  increase in agricultural side activities, as well as amelioration of livelihood.  In particular it’s possible to note that:  -  At an economic level: before the start of this project there were no trade  activities in the area, while now there are many shops and the exchange and  sale of goods it’s significantly improved.   -  At a nutritional level: the local people were used to eat millet every day  and rise and meat only once per month. Now the locals can eat rise and meat  once a week which has improved the nutritional conditions.:  | 0: 0

The local population is very poor, they live managing a few of agricultural  activities, with traditional tools and methods. The most problems affecting to  growth of crops are due to lack of water.  The local people are usually cultivating only millet and peanuts, which are the  main crops in the area, with the consequently problems of a diversified diet and  malnutrition, especially for the children.  Jatropha cultivation can be very useful in bringing an agricultural reformation by  revitalizing land use and livelihoods in rural areas, especially for countries  having abundant barren land and poor in other natural endowments; these  projects, in fact, are creating new job opportunities, preventing land  abandonment and reducing in-country migration to the cities. Among the rural  areas already involved in project activities, there has been registered an  increase in agricultural side activities, as well as amelioration of livelihood. Among the rural  areas already involved in project activities, there has been registered an  increase in agricultural side activities, as well as amelioration of livelihood. The total area of forest land under sustainable management practices is at least 571.33 ha (Document: VERIF_REP_1071_03JUN2009_02JUN2013.pdf, Page: 21). However, the percentage of forest areas certified under recognized sustainable forest management standards is unknown due to the lack of supporting evidence. The types of forest management practices being implemented include sustainable agricultural and forest management practices, agro-forestry practices, regeneration of degraded soils, protection against erosion processes, and saving existing carbon stocks. The key factors influencing the adoption of sustainable forest management practices among forest landowners/operators include the provision of training courses for local farmers on sustainable agricultural and forest management practices, the empowerment of local communities to develop sustainable agro-forestry practices, and the promotion of alternative income sources for local stakeholders through the cultivation of crops such as Jatropha curcas. The average annual rate of increase in the area of forest land under sustainable management practices is unknown due to the lack of supporting evidence.

The context also mentions that carbon stock in the below-ground biomass pool is expected to increase due to the implementation of the project activity (Document: PROJ_DESC_1071_11NOV2013.pdf, Page: 36).
